data.description:
tests/integration/api/meta.test.ts:149-150 carries a docstring that is factually wrong about this repo's own history, in a repo that is public:

  * The document used to state that mutations carry `ETag`/`If-Match` optimistic
  * concurrency; two of two hundred did.

It did not state that at the base of the PR that added this comment. MRQ-146 had already narrowed the sentence to 'Strong `ETag`/`If-Match` optimistic concurrency currently applies only to the two agenda item mutation operations that require it' (commit 5441cf1c). The overclaim the comment describes was fixed one ticket earlier; the PR that wrote this comment was rewriting an already-correct sentence.

This is small, but it is the specific failure mode CLAUDE.md's skill-writing rule names — a comment that rationalizes the present against a past the reader has no way to check, and that in this case did not happen. Someone reading the test to understand why the assertion is shaped that way is told a false story about the codebase.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The docstring describes what the test guards NOW — that info.description's concurrency claim is held to the route table — with no narrative about what the document 'used to' say.
2. No other comment introduced by the same change carries the same false history; check the surrounding block.
3. No assertion changes. This is comment-only; the contract the test enforces is correct and recently strengthened by PR #158.

Files: tests/integration/api/meta.test.ts (:145-155).

Provenance: finding 6 of the 8-finding post-merge review on MRQ-150.
data.title: The OpenAPI concurrency test's docstring tells a history that never happened

provenance.reason: Finding 6 of the PR #136 post-merge review; survived PR #158 and is still on main

data.reason: The cited 5441cf1c is MRQ-148 and not the MRQ-146 OpenAPI change; choose whether this citation mismatch should stop MRQ-161 or allow the verified 32f9a696 history.

data.body: Stopped before editing: the substantive history is confirmed, but the cited commit is wrong in this checkout. git show 5441cf1c identifies MRQ-148 auto-placement and does not touch src/api/openapi.ts; git show 32f9a696 is MRQ-146 and contains the exact narrowed concurrency sentence. The MRQ-150 commit 831867bf adds the disputed comment while that narrowed sentence is already present. Awaiting direction whether to proceed using 32f9a696 or treat the citation mismatch as a stop condition.

Citation corrected — the agent is right and I was wrong.

Verified independently: 'git show --stat 5441cf1c -- src/api/openapi.ts' is empty (MRQ-148, no OpenAPI change), and 'git log -S' on the narrowed sentence returns 32f9a696 'Fix MRQ-146 agent surface honesty' as its introduction, with b95fa130 (PR #136) as its removal.

What I did to produce the bad citation: I read the file with 'git show 5441cf1c:src/api/openapi.ts', which shows the file STATE AT that commit — the PR's merge base, where the narrowed sentence was indeed already present. I then wrote that hash into the ticket as though it were the MRQ-146 commit. State-at-a-commit is not the-commit-that-changed-it, and I collapsed the two.

The substantive claim is unaffected and stands: the narrowed sentence was already in place before the PR that added the disputed docstring, so that docstring describes a history that did not happen.

Corrected citation for the ticket: MRQ-146 narrowed the sentence in 32f9a696; the base of the PR carrying the bad docstring was 5441cf1c, where the narrowed sentence was already present; b95fa130 replaced it.

DIRECTION: proceed with the edit using 32f9a696. Clearing needs-human.

Validation: N/A for running-system/browser validation because MRQ-161 changes only test JSDoc prose; no application behavior or assertions changed. Focused meta.test.ts passed 7/7, and the full pre/post suites had the identical 22 known 401 failures in MRQ-139 and MRQ-131.

Outcome: PR #175 opened as a draft against main at 82a514b6. Source change is comment-only in tests/integration/api/meta.test.ts; no assertions or tests changed. Focused meta.test.ts passed 7/7. Pre- and post-edit npm test both had the identical 22 expected 401 failures (8 MRQ-139, 14 MRQ-131), with 146 files and 979 tests passing; post-edit run also exceeded the 45s budget. npm run pr-gate passed types, build, shell truth, design, API, routes, clocks, and schema checks, then failed only at the same hermetic 22-test suite. Validation is N/A for prose-only change. Known issue about the three MRQ-160/161/162-suffixed filenames is documented in the PR and intentionally untouched.

Update: rebased onto f03ed217 (including PR #171), restored the true falsifiable-claim rationale, ran npm ci, and reran the exact-head npm run pr-gate. All checks passed: 148 test files / 1001 tests and trace:ac with zero uncovered claims. The gate reported pass-over-budget at 225.3s versus 120s, timing-only. Force-pushed 4618be9d; PR #175 is now ready for review. GitHub fast-gate is pending on the new head.

Outcome: PR #175 merged via squash at 36d7c8dd. The change is prose-only in tests/integration/api/meta.test.ts: the true falsifiable-claim rationale remains, the false historical backstory is removed, and no assertions or tests changed. Exact-head npm run pr-gate after rebasing onto f03ed217 passed all checks: 148 test files / 1001 tests, trace:ac reported zero uncovered claims; pass-over-budget at 225.3s versus the 120s timing budget was timing-only. GitHub fast-gate passed. The three MRQ-160/MRQ-161/MRQ-162 filename collisions remain documented and intentionally untouched. No deployment performed.
